This project studies silicon nitride membranes combined with graphene, MoS₂, and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN).

## Research question

How do fabrication routes, material interfaces, and nanoscale geometry influence device behavior and directional molecular transport?

## Approach and contributions

I applied and adapted the laboratory’s previously developed **chemically tuned controlled dielectric breakdown (CT-CDB)** method to heterogeneous multilayer devices. Fabrication and electrical characterization covered five architectures:

- SiNₓ/graphene
- SiNₓ/MoS₂
- SiNₓ/hBN
- SiNₓ/graphene/MoS₂
- SiNₓ/graphene/hBN

Comparative experiments examined directional transport through these structures. Numerical modeling and quantitative signal analysis investigated electric-field distributions and transport behavior, with machine learning supporting structural classification of experimental signals.
